content.text: {"primary_meaning": "In Christian teaching and biblical interpretation, a 'name' symbolizes the essential character, identity, and authority of the person who bears it — not merely a label. Above all, the 'name of God' (or 'the name of the LORD' / 'the name of Jesus') stands for God's revealed nature, reputation, presence, and power, so that to know, call on, trust, hallow, or act 'in' the name is to engage with the person himself. Names in Scripture are consistently treated as disclosing or determining who someone truly is, which is why God's self-revelation, divine name-changes, and prayer/salvation 'in the name' carry such theological weight.", "primary_basis": ["Exodus 3:13-15 (God reveals his name 'I AM WHO I AM' / YHWH as self-disclosure of his being)", "Exodus 34:5-7 (the LORD 'proclaimed the name of the LORD' by declaring his character: merciful, gracious, etc.)", "Exodus 20:7 / Deuteronomy 5:11 (prohibition against taking the LORD's name in vain, treating the name as bound to God's honor)", "Psalm 9:10 ('those who know your name put their trust in you')", "Proverbs 18:10 ('the name of the LORD is a strong tower')", "Matthew 6:9 ('hallowed be your name' in the Lord's Prayer)", "John 17:6, 26 (Jesus manifests/makes known the Father's name)", "Philippians 2:9-11 (God gives Jesus 'the name that is above every name')", "Acts 4:12 ('no other name under heaven... by which we must be saved')", "Joel 2:32 / Acts 2:21 / Romans 10:13 ('everyone who calls on the name of the Lord will be saved')", "Genesis 17:5 and 32:28 (name changes — Abram to Abraham, Jacob to Israel — marking new identity and destiny)", "Isaiah 9:6 ('his name shall be called Wonderful Counselor...' — name as description of character)"], "alternatives": [{"meaning": "Name as delegated authority and agency: to speak, act, baptize, heal, or pray 'in the name of' someone is to act by their authorization and power (e.g., prayer in Jesus' name, baptism in the triune name).", "basis": ["John 14:13-14", "Matthew 28:19", "Acts 3:6, 16", "Colossians 3:17", "1 Samuel 17:45"], "prominence": "common"}, {"meaning": "Name as God's manifest presence and dwelling ('Name theology'): in Deuteronomistic texts God causes his 'name to dwell' in the sanctuary, so the name functions as a mode of divine presence among his people; developed in critical scholarship and echoed in theology of the temple.", "basis": ["Deuteronomy 12:5, 11", "1 Kings 8:27-29", "2 Chronicles 7:16", "Jeremiah 7:12"], "prominence": "common"}, {"meaning": "Name as reputation, honor, fame, or memorial: a 'good name' or 'great name' signifies standing and remembrance, and God acts 'for his name's sake' to vindicate his reputation.", "basis": ["Proverbs 22:1", "Ecclesiastes 7:1", "Genesis 11:4", "Genesis 12:2", "2 Samuel 7:9", "Ezekiel 36:22-23", "Psalm 23:3"], "prominence": "common"}, {"meaning": "Naming as an act of dominion or sovereignty: the one who names exercises authority over what is named (Adam naming the animals; conquerors renaming subjects).", "basis": ["Genesis 2:19-20", "Genesis 1:5, 8, 10", "Daniel 1:7", "2 Kings 24:17"], "prominence": "common"}, {"meaning": "The 'new name' as symbol of redeemed identity, eschatological belonging, and transformation of the believer.", "basis": ["Revelation 2:17", "Revelation 3:12", "Isaiah 62:2", "Isaiah 56:5"], "prominence": "common"}, {"meaning": "Names written in the 'book of life' or on the person as symbols of election, ownership, and covenant membership.", "basis": ["Revelation 3:5", "Revelation 13:8", "Revelation 14:1", "Revelation 22:4", "Luke 10:20"], "prominence": "common"}, {"meaning": "Sacred Name readings: the specific pronounced Hebrew name (Yahweh/YHWH) itself carries intrinsic power or is required for true worship and salvation (Sacred Name movement and related groups).", "basis": ["Exodus 3:15", "Psalm 68:4", "Joel 2:32 (read as requiring the Hebrew name)"], "prominence": "rare"}, {"meaning": "Individual biblical names read allegorically or etymologically as prophetic of the bearer's role or of Christ (e.g., Jesus/Yeshua = 'YHWH saves'; Isaiah's sign-children; patristic name-allegory).", "basis": ["Matthew 1:21", "Isaiah 7:14 and 8:1-4", "Hosea 1:4-9", "Genesis 5 genealogy readings in devotional literature"], "prominence": "minority"}], "has_settled_consensus": true, "confidence": "high", "notes": "There is broad, well-recognized consensus across Catholic, Orthodox, Protestant, and academic biblical scholarship that 'name' in Scripture symbolizes the person's character, identity, presence, and authority — supremely so for the name of God and of Jesus. The listed alternatives are largely complementary facets (authority, presence, reputation, dominion, new identity) rather than rival readings, and standard reference works (e.g., Bible dictionaries, TDNT/TDOT entries on shem/onoma) treat them together under the same core concept. The chief genuinely divergent position is the Sacred Name insistence on the phonetic Hebrew name itself, which is a fringe view. 'Name theology' as a distinct scholarly construct (name as hypostasis-like presence) is debated in academic circles but does not disturb the popular consensus."}
